messages.aboutText: Vulman is an all-in-one vulnerability management local desktop application for your coding projects and infrastructure. It is highly secure and uses AES-GCM encryption to keep vulnerability results in a local database. Vulman never stores your code or infrastructure data in its database or data directory, and it never passes any of it to any 3rd party. Only vulnerability detection and code-scanning results are kept in the Vulman local database using AES-GCM encryption, and the encryption key is stored in the Vulman local data directory as vulman.key.
messages.aboutArchitecture: Vulman is written in Go and JavaScript with an embedded, encrypted bbolt database. It uses Go Wails architecture to build the native UI. Because of the architecture, Vulman is very lightweight and relatively fast.
messages.aboutGiftMessage: If you can find a security hole in Vulman that lets Vulman record and maliciously send local data to a 3rd party, I will buy you a coffee. Please get in touch with us through Vulman's public repository to get the coffee bill:

messages.scannerInstallCommand: Install with this command or follow the guide.
messages.scannerGoInstall: Install Go, run the command below, and add GOBIN (or the bin folder under GOPATH) to PATH.
messages.scannerGoInstallMac: Install Go, then run the command below. Vulman searches the default Go bin folder.
messages.scannerPipAuditInstall: Install Python and pipx using the guide, then run the command below. Use pipx ensurepath to add the executable to PATH.
messages.scannerNodeWindows: Install the Windows Node.js LTS package, which includes npm.
messages.scannerComposerWindows: Install PHP, then run Composer-Setup.exe and select the PHP executable.
messages.scannerTrivyWindows: Extract the Windows release archive and put the folder containing trivy.exe on PATH.
messages.scannerTrivyRepository: Follow the guide to add Trivy’s signed package repository, then run the command below.
messages.scannerSnykWindows: Download the standalone Windows CLI and rename it to snyk.exe.
messages.scannerSnykLinux: Download the standalone Linux CLI for your architecture, rename it to snyk, and give it execute permission.
messages.scannerSnykInstall: Install the Snyk CLI and make it available on Vulman’s PATH. Vulman runs snyk test to check project dependencies.
messages.scannerSnykSetup: Copy your API token from Snyk account settings or use a Snyk personal access token. Paste it into API credentials → Snyk token, select Snyk here, and save the configuration.
messages.scannerSnykProject: In Edit project, add a GitHub repository URL or local folder and enable Run configured code scanners. Save the project, then select Scan code.
messages.scannerSnykReady: Vulman can run the Snyk CLI. Snyk checks the token during a scan.
messages.snykTokenHint: Vulman passes this token to the Snyk CLI as SNYK_TOKEN to authenticate dependency scans.
messages.scannerInstallGeneric: Follow the guide for your system and add the executable’s directory to PATH.
messages.scannerPathDarwin: Vulman searches the standard Homebrew and Go folders. For a custom location, start Vulman’s executable from a terminal that can find the tool on PATH.
messages.scannerPathWindows: Include the tool and any required runtime in your user Path under Environment Variables, then reopen Vulman.
messages.scannerPathLinux: Include the executable’s folder in PATH, then reopen Vulman from the same environment.
messages.scannerPermissionsUnix: Give your account execute permission on the trusted file (for example, chmod u+x on a file you own) and access to its parent directories. Use a location that allows executables.
messages.scannerPermissionsDarwin: If macOS blocked a verified installation, check System Settings → Privacy & Security.
messages.scannerPermissionsWindows: In the executable’s Properties → Security, check that your account has Read & execute access. Contact your administrator if an organizational policy blocks it.
